Cyberdreigingen voor: Waarom dit nu prio: Cyber threats for: Why this must be a priority now The progress report of the Nationaal Cyber Security Centrum (NCSA) (Open Overheid) reports that the Netherlands is participating in large-scale, government-wide cyber exercises such as Cyber Europe. Such exercises show that cyber threats are not only technical, but test governance decision-making and cooperation between agencies and suppliers. For entrepreneurs this means: external signals change rapidly and can impact strategy, cash flows, processes, people and reputation. You cannot only react to incidents; you must close the chain from signals to decisions.
1) Signaal: wat je moet volgen en hoe je: 1) Signal: what you should monitor and how you measure it - What: external signals (government advisories and exercises such as Cyber Europe, vulnerability notifications from suppliers, sector incidents) and internal signals (unexplained outages, unusual network activity, employee reports). - Supporting evidence: the NCSA progress report indicates that government-wide exercises take place and that collaboration and exercising are central. Use this as a reason to signal structurally. - Owner: IT responsible or CISO (for smaller companies: IT manager). - Metric: a fixed dashboard with newly received external warnings and internal security alerts (daily feed). Output = number of prioritized signals per week.
2) Context & gevolg: vertaal signalen na: 2) Context & consequence: translate signals into business impact - What: place each signal in business context: which systems, customer processes, revenue streams, regulations (compliance) and suppliers does this affect? - Owner: CISO/IT + responsible line manager (e.g. commercial or operations) with the CFO involved for financial impact. - Metric: a one-page impact analysis per signal (who, what, when) that is approved by the responsible line manager within 48 hours.
3) Beslissing: wie beslist en op basis v: 3) Decision: who decides and on what criteria - What: decide whether the incident/risk: a) requires immediate isolation/intervention, b) deserves planned remediation, or c) is acceptable with compensation/insurance handling. - Owner: CEO/MT for strategic choices; delegated authority: CISO/IT manager for operational decisions within agreed budgets. - Metric: decisions are recorded with: chosen option, budget limit and deadline. Time between signal and decision should be visible.
4) Actie: concrete taken, eigenaar en ko: 4) Action: concrete tasks, owner and costs - What: technical fixes (patch, isolation), process actions (customer communication), contract actions (supplier briefing), and people actions (extra instruction/shift staff). - Owner: operational task owners: IT operations (patching), HR (phishing communication), Customer Service (briefing customers), Procurement (supplier meeting). - Metrics: action checklist with status (open/doing/done), time to execution from decision, and budget consumption per action.
5) Resultaat & controleerbare uitkomst -: 5) Result & verifiable outcome - What: what did the action deliver? Was the incident contained, is the service restored, were customers correctly informed, were contractual requirements met? - Owner: owner of the original decision and the functional lead who executed the action. - Measurement: closure report with KPIs such as: incident status (closed/mitigated/ongoing), time to recovery, number of affected customers contacted and follow-up measures.
6) Leren: update beleid, processen en bu: 6) Learning: update policy, processes and budgeting - What: after the action a brief after-action review: what went well, what didn’t, which decisions failed or lacked information? - Owner: MT + CISO. - Metrics: update of playbooks, training for involved staff, and a priority list with financial estimate for the next quarterly budget.
Het gesloten verbeterproces (de bestuurl: The closed improvement process (the governance loop) Use one simple, repeatable loop: signal → context → consequence → decision → action → result → learning. Below I explain what each element practically means for your company, who gets clear ownership, and which concrete outcome you can measure.

Concreet 6-stappen implementatieplan voo: Concrete 6-step implementation plan for the next 90 days 1) Asset and dependency map (week 1–3) - Owner: CTO/CIO. - Output: one auditable register of critical systems, data flows and suppliers, approved by CFO. 2) Signal-feed & triage (week 1–4) - Owner: IT-manager. - Output: configured feed and daily triage; measurable: % of signals assessed within 24 hours. 3) Impact template & decision rules (week 2–6) - Owner: CISO with MT. - Output: standard impact analysis and decision tree (who decides at which level) with approval from CEO. 4) Tabletop exercise (week 6–8) - Owner: MT (initiative CEO), facilitated by IT/CISO. - Output: exercise report with concrete actions, responsibilities and improvement points — record this in your board dossier. - Source advice: NCSA recommends regular exercises as part of national preparedness and cooperation. 5) Operationalize fixes and communication (week 8–12) - Owner: IT-operations and Customer Service. - Output: implemented fixes and customer communication; measurable: actions in checklist are 'done' with timestamps. 6) After-action review and budgeting (week 12) - Owner: MT + CFO. - Output: updated playbook, training plan and budget proposal for the next quarter.
Verbind strategie, geld en risico: besli: Connect strategy, money and risk: decision format for the board - Decision format: signal-ID + short impact analysis + option A/B/C + estimated cost + recommended owner + deadline. - Decision rule: do we take a structural investment (capex/opex) if the unweighted probability*impact is greater than the acceptance threshold the MT has set? Record the threshold in euro's or reputation levels.
Eigenaarschap en governance (kort) - Str: Ownership and governance (brief) - Strategic ownership: CEO/MT — decisions on investment, customer communication and reputation. - Financial ownership: CFO — budget allocation and insurance. - Operational ownership: CISO/IT-manager — detection, mitigation and patching. - People & training: HR — awareness, phishing tests and crisis communication roles.
Afsluitend bewijs en waarom oefenen werk: Concluding evidence and why exercises work The NCSA report shows that governments exercise at scale; the same principle applies to companies: exercises force ownership, establish decision routes and reveal weak spots. Use that government approach as a trigger: exercises and board-level readability are not a luxury; they are risk-management products that link strategy and spending to concrete outcomes.
Wat je vandaag concreet kunt doen (kort): What you can do concretely today (brief) - Gather your MT for a 90-min tabletop using the 6-step plan above. - During that session, immediately assign owners for the asset register, signal-feed and impact template. - Record decisions and metrics in a single simple board dossier.
Door deze aanpak verbind je externe sign: With this approach you connect external signals to governance choices, concrete actions and measurable outcomes — thereby closing the loop needed to make cyber threats manageable.
Gebruik Cyberdreigingen voor niet als pa: Do not treat cyber threats as a paper tick-box: assess the actual situation, test the criteria and record the chosen action.
Vier vaste controlepunten voor Cyberdrei: Four fixed checkpoints for cyber threats: facts, agreements, risk and evidence. That keeps the assessment reproducible.
